title: Ascending Flags – Portfolio Page
description: Economy architecture, a 40+ card catalog and cross-discipline leadership on a competitive card game at Scary Noodles.

blocks.html:
Page draft for the portfolio. Lines marked ASSET are things for you to find; brackets are facts to confirm. This project had no Wix page, so it needs the most input from you.

Card Game · Scary Noodles · Published · Apr – Sep 2023

Conceived and led a published card game where movement, attack and defence all compete for one shared pool of mana.

rows: Game Designer, concept and design lead

blocks.text: 1. One pool of mana for everything

blocks.html:
Many card games give separate resources for different actions. Here, moving, attacking and defending all draw from the same mana pool, so every turn is a trade-off: spending to advance leaves less to protect yourself.

[embedded content: mana economy · one pool, three uses\]

Example turn \[fill in from the game\]: "With \[X\] mana, a player can \[move two spaces and attack once\] or \[defend fully and move once\]. Neither is right every time; it depends on \[the board state\]."

ASSET – Annotated turn: a screenshot of one turn with callouts showing the choice the player faces.

I designed and documented every card, and kept the catalogue organized so art and engineering always worked from the current version. I also designed the board.

ASSET – Card spread: 5 cards side by side, one of each type. ASSET – Card catalogue screenshot: your spreadsheet or document listing the cards.

blocks.text: 3. Testing on paper and in simulation

blocks.html:
I validated the concept with paper prototypes before any engine work, then balanced it with spreadsheets and Machinations simulations of the mana economy, and used playtests to find balance problems the models missed.

ASSET – Paper prototype photo and a Machinations diagram screenshot. A Machinations diagram is rare in portfolios and shows systems thinking at once.

Your master CV says fog of war improved the experience by 60%. That's a strong claim, so the page needs the story behind it.

  • Problem: \[what wasn't working in playtests: for example, players could see everything and planned too far ahead, or matches felt solved early\]
  • Cause: \[why\]
  • Fix: I designed a fog-of-war feature that \[what it hides or reveals, and how players uncover it\].
  • Result: \[what changed, and what the 60% measures: survey scores between rounds? If you can't say how it was measured, describe the change without the number.\]

ASSET – Fog of war before/after: the same board with and without fog.

I led design, art and engineering through close collaboration for the whole project, owned the backlog and roadmap, and set feature priorities. I built spreadsheets that made handoffs between departments faster.
